title: Salted Caramel and Toasted Coconut Ice Cream (No Egg)
changes_from_base: A dark homemade salted caramel flavours the base and is rippled through, with toasted coconut folded in, instead of strawberries.
summary: Dark homemade salted caramel flavours the base and runs through it in ribbons, while toasted coconut adds a nutty crunch.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
light corn syrup or glucose syrup

steps.title: Caramel
steps.text: Melt the 150 g sugar in the small heavy pan over medium heat, swirling rather than stirring, until it turns a deep amber, about 180 °C. Off the heat, pour in the warm cream carefully (it will bubble up hard), then stir in the butter and salt until smooth.

steps.title: Divide
steps.text: Pour a third of the caramel into the heatproof bowl and leave it to cool for the swirl.

steps.title: Base
steps.text: Warm the 330 ml cream, the milk, 40 g sugar and syrup in the medium saucepan until the sugar dissolves, then whisk in the rest of the warm caramel and the vanilla. Cool, then chill for at least 4 h.

steps.title: Toast the coconut
steps.text: Stir the coconut in the dry frying pan over medium-low heat for 3-4 min until golden and fragrant, then tip onto a plate to cool.

steps.title: Churn and swirl
steps.text: Churn the caramel base for 20-30 min, then fold in the coconut. Layer it into the container with spoonfuls of the reserved caramel and drag a knife through once or twice for ribbons. Freeze for at least 4 h.

tips: Take the caramel dark, to a deep amber; pale caramel tastes only sweet.
Warm the cream before adding it to the caramel so it splutters less and does not seize.
The reserved caramel thickens as it cools; warm it for a few seconds if it is too stiff to swirl.
storage: Keep covered with baking paper pressed on the surface in the freezer for up to 2 weeks. Soften for 10 min in the fridge before scooping.
